LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To give and follow simple directions and instructions.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.

3.– WORKSHEET: IS THAT RIGHT OR WRONG? (P.7) (8’)
Is That Right or Wrong?
7
NOTE: if you collected your Ss books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
MATERIALS
•	 Pencils or crayons 
This worksheet depicts a map like the one used in Activity 
3, but with some variations. The Ss must compare the map in 
their student book to the A3 map and spot the differences. The 
A3 map is the correct version of the map and should be used as 
reference. Place the A3 in the middle of the table or on a wall 
close to where the Ss are sitting so that they can see it easily.
Quickly review the concepts right or wrong with your students 
by asking them questions about themselves like, “John is 12 
years old. Is that right or wrong?” to which students should 
then reply, “No, that’s wrong. John is 8 years old.”
Then, explain to the Ss that they must take it in turns to spot 
what is wrong on their map in their student book. Have all the 
students look at the map in their student book, then ask the 
following questions:
KEY (Answers may vary)
•	 The charity shop is opposite the newsagent’s, is that 
right or wrong? It’s wrong! 
•	 Where is the charity shop? The charity shop is opposite 
the pet shop.
•	 The cafe is next to the greengrocer’s, is that right 
or wrong? It’s wrong!

•	 Where is the café? The café is next to the hospital.
•	 The swimming pool is behind the sweet shop, is that 
right or wrong? It’s wrong! 
•	 Where is the swimming pool? The swimming pool is 
next to the animal shelter.
•	 The ice cream parlour is opposite the shoe shop, is 
that right or wrong? It’s wrong! 
•	 Where is the ice cream parlour? The ice cream parlour 
is opposite the football pitch.
•	 The animal shelter is between the ice cream parlour 
and the football pitch, is that right or wrong? It’s 
wrong! 
•	 Where is the animal shelter? The animal shelter is 
opposite the shoe shop.
•	 The pet shop is next to the bank, is that right or 
wrong? It’s wrong! 
•	 Where is the pet shop? The pet shop is next to the 
town hall.
•	 The town hall is in front of the petrol station, is that 
right or wrong? It’s wrong! 
•	 Where is the town hall? The town hall is between the 
pet shop and the football pitch.
•	 The sports centre is opposite the library, is that right 
or wrong? It’s wrong!
•	 Where is the sports centre? The sports centre is 
opposite the toyshop. 
Have the Ss cross out the incorrect shops on their student 
book. Try to ask each S a question.
> Advanced Groups
Ss can also play the teacher’s role by asking their classmates, 
for example, “Jane, look! The school is next to the dentist; is 
that right or wrong?” and then, Jane should reply accordingly, 
“Yes, that’s right. The school is next to the dentist.”

5.– ACTIVITY 1: CHARACTER MATCHING (7’)
P.2.1
P.2.1
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the actions that each character is doing by 
putting the Place cards (P.2.1) down on the table. Say, “Grandpa 
and Grandma are going to the doctor’s, Mum is going to the 
hairdresser’s, and Dad is doing the gardening.”
Show the Ss the X cards and ask, “Why can’t Mum take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop?”, to which they should reply, 
“Because she is going to the hairdresser’s.” Continue in this 
manner until you have gone over all the pairs.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
To introduce the activity, say, “Let’s see if you remember 
what Pam and Paul’s family are doing!”. Put the P.2.1 cards 
in two piles face down: X cards on one side, Place cards on 
the other. The Ss must flip a card from each pile to match the 
character with the correct reason for them to not be able to 
take Pam and Paul to the toyshop.
If they have a match, they should say, “Mum can’t take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop, because she is going to the 
hairdresser’s. I’ve got a pair!” If they don’t, they should say 
“I’ve got Grandpa and Grandma and doing the gardening; it’s 
not a pair, what a shame!” 
> Correct matches and structures
•	 Mum + going to the hairdresser’s: “Mum (she) can’t take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop because she is going to 
the hairdresser’s.”
•	 Dad + doing the gardening: “Dad (he) can’t take Pam and 
Paul to the toyshop because he is doing the gardening.”

•	 Grandma and Grandpa + going to the doctor’s: “Grandma 
and Grandpa (they) can’t take Pam and Paul to the 
toyshop because they are going to the doctor’s.” 
> Follow-Up
Quickly split the group into two teams. Show team A the X 
card and team B the matching place card. Each team should 
say the part of the structure corresponding to their card. For 
example:
•	 Team A: “Grandpa and Grandma can’t take Pam and 
Paul to the toyshop...” 
•	 Team B: “...because they are going to the doctor’s.” 
6.– ACTIVITY 7: DIRECTIONS SONG (TR#13) 
(VERSION 1) (3’)
> Main Activity
To perform the song, have the Ss stand with their back against 
the wall in a line, side by side. Then the first time they sing the 
song they will simply turn left and right while standing in place 
and then walk straight ahead when the song says to do so.
The second time you do the activity, they must line up behind 
one another forming a train, holding onto the shoulders of the 
S in front of them. Then, this time, when the song says turn left 
and right, they will actually walk around the room while doing 
so. The song will speed up so make sure the Ss are ready to 
do the actions quickly.
DIRECTIONS SONG
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead
Straight, straight, straight
That was great! Now line up! Ready? Steady? Go! 
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead
Straight, straight, straight
(repeat) 
Very good! Now let’s go faster!
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead

Straight, straight, straight
(repeat)
7.– ACTIVITY 5: SHOPPING LISTS (VERSION 2) (8’) 
P.2.5
P.2.5
> How to Play
In this game, Ss need to find three shops where they can 
buy the items on their shopping list.
> Warm-Up
Go over the items that can be bought at the shops using the 
Shopping Lists cards (P.2.5). Ask them, for example, “Where 
can you buy boots?” to which Ss must answer, “You can buy 
boots at the shoe shop.”
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “It’s time to go shopping! 
Let’s see if you can buy all the items on your shopping list!”. 
Give one Shopping List card (P.2.5) to each S. The Ss should keep 
their shopping lists face up on the table in front of them. Pick one 
card of each shop (13 in total: supermarket, butcher’s, bakery, 
café, shoe shop, clothes shop, greengrocer’s, fishmonger’s, 
toyshop, newsagent’s, bookshop, ice cream parlour, pet shop) 
and mix the deck.
Hold it in the palm of your hand and start putting the cards 
face down on a pile in the middle of the table. Ss must take it 
in turns to say, “Stop!”, and flip over the last card you placed 
on the deck. Then, they need to identify the shop by saying, for 
example, “It’s the ice cream parlour.”. Whoever has ice cream 
on their card needs to say, “You can buy ice cream at the ice 
cream parlour!”. You should then mark the shopping list of 
all the Ss who have that item. You can either use counters or 
your board marker. 
Every time a Ss flips a card, take it out of the deck and leave 
it aside.

The game finishes when you have run out of time, or when 
a S has completed their shopping list.
> Follow-Up
Ask the two Ss who finished first to describe their shopping 
list as follows:
•	 You can buy tomatoes at the greengrocer’s.
•	 You can buy boots at the shoe shop.
•	 You can buy fish at the fishmonger’s.
8.– ACTIVITY 6: FREEZE! (5’)
P.2.5
> Main Activity
The Ss sit on the floor in a circle. Tell them, “Let’s see if 
you remember what you can buy at each shop!”. Place the 
pile of Shop cards (P.2.5) face down in the middle of the circle 
and get the Ss to begin passing the ball. Tell them that when 
you say “Freeze!”, they must stop. Whenever you feel like it, 
shout out “FREEZE!” and the S holding the ball must pick up 
a card from the middle of the circle and answer the question, 
“What can you buy at the…?” as quickly as possible. Once Ss 
are used to the game you can make it more dynamic by not 
asking them the question and letting them come up with the 
sentence themselves. For example: 
•	 You can buy jumpers at the clothes shop.
•	 You can buy video games at the toy shop.
•	 You can buy muffins at the bakery.
NOTE: you can also play songs from the story to make it 
more dynamic. You can still say “Freeze!” every time you pause 
the song.

9.– ACTIVITY 9: NUMBERS (VERSION 1) (5’)
P.E.M.3
55
> Main Activity
The goal of the game is to find as many cards as possible. 
Stick some of the Number cards (P.E.M.3.) on the wall (out 
of reach of the Ss, so they can’t damage them). Say, “Find 
number...” and have the Ss run and point to the corresponding 
number. When the S points to the correct number, take it off 
the wall and keep it as a point for that S. The S who collects 
the most cards wins.
NOTE: this game can become hectic if everybody is playing 
at the same time. It is advisable to play this game in duels of 
two Ss (S1 vs S2). You call out the number and the two Ss must 
race to point to the card first.

11.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’) 
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class. 
BONUS
ACTIVITY 8: TAKE A WALK (VERSION 2) (TR#15) 
P.2.5
> How to Play
This version of this activity is played like the musical chairs 
game.
Stick up the Shop cards (P.2.5) that appear in Take a Walk 
Version 2 (TR#15) (pet shop, ice cream parlour, clothes shop, 
toyshop and bakery) around the room. Look at the lyrics and 
try not to place the shops that are sung one after another too 
close together.
> Warm-Up
If you feel it is necessary, quickly drill the names of the 
different shops or places.
To do this without taking the cards off the wall, walk around 
the room and ask Ss to shout out the different names saying, 
“It’s the clothes shop! It’s the bakery!”, etc.
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s take a walk around 
town!”. Next, play the song Take A Walk Version 2 (TR#15). 
Ss must sing along to the song and walk around the room and 
when they hear one of the shops or places being mentioned, 
they must go and point to that place.
During the musical interlude, encourage Ss to ask, “Where 
shall we go next?”

> Follow-Up
If time allows, ask each S, “What can you buy at the...?” 
and the Ss individually, each saying a different item, should 
say, “You can buy ... at the...”. Challenge them to come up with 
items they haven’t learned in class.

ACTIVITY 4: FOLLOWING DIRECTIONS
> Warm-Up
Put a red sticker on each Ss’ left hand and a green one on 
their right. Then practise left, right and straight ahead by using 
your hands. Say, “Turn left!” and have everybody turn to the left 
(you should too; having your back turned to your Ss is helpful, 
so everybody is pointing to the same left). Do the same with 
right and straight ahead.
Gradually say each command faster and faster.
> Main Activity
Next, the Ss should form a line. When you say, “Go straight 
ahead”, they must pat the person in front of them on the head. If 
you say, “Turn left” Ss must pat the left shoulder of the person 
in front of them and if you say, “Turn right”, their right shoulder. 
Finally, get them (still in a line) to follow your instructions 
but walking around the class pretending to be on a train.
> Advanced Groups
If your Ss have understood the concepts quickly, you can 
let them take on the teacher role and give commands to their 
classmates.
